channel.title: Daily Digest
channel.description: Curated tech blog summaries, inspired by Andrej Karpathy's reading list

item.title: My blog has moved
item.description: The author provides a notice that their blog has migrated to a new platform. They include a link to the new location and provide an updated RSS feed for existing subscribers to follow.

item.title: Kort geding aandeelhouders Solvinity
item.description: The author recounts their firsthand observations from the Solvinity shareholders' lawsuit against the Dutch government regarding a blocked sale to a US firm. They note discrepancies between the courtroom events and the subsequent media coverage by major news outlets.

item.title: A full body MRI earns you a year of smoking
item.description: This article explores the concept of radiation exposure by equating the dosage received from a full-body MRI to equivalent risks in other activities. It uses provocative comparisons to put medical imaging risks into perspective against common or extreme life experiences.

item.title: Content addressing in package managers
item.description: This article explores the implementation of content addressing in modern package managers, where data is identified by cryptographic hashes rather than locations. It surveys various systems that utilize content-addressable storage for files, layers, and artifacts to improve deduplication, security, and verification.

item.title: How did Windows 95 decide that a setup program ran?
item.description: This post explains the technical heuristics used by Windows 95 to identify when a setup program was running. It provides historical insight into the operating system's internal detection mechanisms.

item.title: Pluralistic: How US states and international trustbusters can beat Big Tech (07 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: This article examines the global trend of antitrust enforcement against Big Tech, highlighting the collaborative efforts between US regulators and international authorities. It posits that a shared commitment to aggressive antitrust policy is essential to curbing the power of major technology corporations.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0, now with database schema migrations
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0, a major update introducing database schema migrations, nested transactions, and support for compound foreign keys. The release highlights the powerful table.transform() method, which enables complex schema modifications beyond standard SQLite capabilities.

item.title: sqlite-migrate 0.2
item.description: The sqlite-migrate library has been updated to version 0.2, which officially retires the standalone package. It now functions as a compatibility shim to support the newly released sqlite-utils 4.0 dependency.

item.title: github-code Web Component
item.description: Simon Willison introduces an experimental Web Component, github-code, created using AI to embed specific sections of GitHub files into web pages. The tool fetches raw code from GitHub based on provided URLs and renders it with line numbers.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0
item.description: sqlite-utils 4.0 has been released, introducing support for database schema migrations. This update enhances the tool's capabilities for managing and evolving SQLite database structures.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc4
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0rc4, which serves as the final release candidate before the stable 4.0 version. This update primarily incorporates feedback provided during a detailed review by Claude Fable 5.

item.title: tencent/Hy3
item.description: Tencent has released Hy3, a new 295B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model featuring a 256K context window and Apache 2.0 licensing. The model demonstrates high performance in productivity tasks and is currently available for testing via OpenRouter.

item.title: Blog about things you don't understand yet
item.description: This article discusses the intellectual benefit of engaging with topics that currently elude your understanding. It highlights the importance of curiosity and the mental growth that comes from tackling complex, unfamiliar subjects.

item.title: GLM 5.2 and the coming AI margin collapse (part 1)
item.description: The article introduces GLM 5.2 as a powerful open-weights model capable of matching top-tier competitors like GPT and Opus for agentic tasks. It suggests that this performance at a significantly lower price point signals an impending collapse in AI inference profit margins.

item.title: Making a Shuffle Button
item.description: The author describes the challenge of implementing a 'Shuffle' button on a static blog, specifically the inefficiencies of embedding all post IDs into every page using JavaScript. He seeks a more performant, non-JS alternative to avoid unnecessary rebuilds and cache invalidation caused by frequent content updates.

item.title: Reproducing a geometry theorem diagram
item.description: The author explores the process of programmatically recreating a specific geometry theorem diagram using coordinates and mathematical assumptions. By defining the unit circle and the perpendicular line CD, the post details the steps taken to plot the geometric components accurately.

item.title: e approximation
item.description: This article explores a highly accurate fractional approximation of the mathematical constant e (2721/1001). It contrasts this specific approximation with simpler methods, highlighting how such fractions can provide greater precision than standard decimal truncations.

item.title: I opened a file with FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE, but now I changed my mind
item.description: This post explains that the FILE_FLAG_DELETE_ON_CLOSE flag cannot be removed once a file is opened with it. It suggests that if you need to retain the file, you must adopt a different approach to file handling.

item.title: Life with hazard ratios
item.description: The article explains why hazard ratios in health studies are often misinterpreted as direct indicators of life expectancy changes. Through the use of hypothetical models like Russian roulette, it demonstrates that the impact of a hazard ratio depends heavily on the baseline mortality rate and the age at which risks occur.

item.title: I'm just so bored of AI
item.description: The author expresses growing fatigue with the constant hype surrounding artificial intelligence, comparing it to repetitive and tedious conversations about fleeting trends. They argue that the novelty of AI-driven automation is quickly wearing off, leading to a sense of exhaustion with current tech discourse.

item.title: Stephan's Quintet
item.description: This post provides a deep-sky analysis of Stephan's Quintet, noting that the blue spiral galaxy is a foreground object rather than a true member of the group. It details the technical configuration and processing workflow used to capture this image of the Hickson Compact Group 92.

item.title: Amazon Basics, but for intellectual property.
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article discusses the conflict of interest inherent in Amazon's business model, where the platform leverages proprietary sales data to replicate successful third-party products under its Amazon Basics brand. It highlights how merchants are forced to expose their operational data to Amazon to reach customers, despite Amazon's denials regarding the misuse of private seller information.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc3
item.description: Simon Willison has released sqlite-utils 4.0rc3, introducing support for compound foreign keys and updated case-insensitive column matching. This release incorporates various bug fixes and improvements as the project nears its stable 4.0 version.

item.title: C2PA only works if everything is signed
item.description: This article examines the limitations of the C2PA standard, arguing that its effectiveness depends entirely on universal adoption and consistent signing across the entire digital content lifecycle. It highlights how gaps in the verification chain can compromise the integrity and trustworthiness of media provenance.

item.title: Travel notes: PLDI Boulder
item.description: Max Bernstein reflects on his fourth PLDI conference experience in Boulder, highlighting the value of networking, research discussions, and workshops. He notes specific technical insights gained from the EGRAPHS workshop and casual interactions with fellow researchers.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2, mostly written by Claude Fable (for about $149.25)
item.description: Simon Willison uses the AI tool Claude Fable to conduct a final code review of sqlite-utils 4.0rc1 before the stable release. The process successfully identified critical bugs, including a serious data integrity issue with delete_where(), helping ensure a more robust version 4.0.

item.title: sqlite-utils 4.0rc2
item.description: Simon Willison has announced the release of sqlite-utils 4.0rc2. A significant portion of this version was developed with the assistance of the AI model Claude Fable.

item.title: Building a World Map with only 500 bytes
item.description: This post highlights an innovative technique for generating an ASCII world map using just 445 bytes of data. It demonstrates how to leverage deflate compression and JavaScript's fetch API with data URIs to achieve highly efficient text rendering.

item.title: Better Models: Worse Tools
item.description: The article discusses a regression where newer Claude models struggle with tool-use schemas compared to older versions. It suggests that models are becoming overly optimized for specific vendor-provided tools, leading to compatibility issues with third-party coding harnesses.

item.title: Reading List 07/04/26
item.description: This digest covers a diverse range of topics, including the prevalence of households without homeowners insurance and the implications of AI chip smuggling. It also explores technical and business developments such as Japan’s unique dual-frequency electrical grid and Meta's current strategy in the AI computing sector.

item.title: This Week in Package Management: 4 July 2026
item.description: This weekly digest covers key updates across various package managers including Hex, Conan, uv, pixi, mise, Rust/Cargo, npm, and Homebrew. The releases focus on security enhancements, dependency policy management, SBOM improvements, and performance optimizations.

item.title: Does additional data always reduce posterior variance?
item.description: This post examines the counterintuitive Bayesian scenario where collecting additional data does not always result in a decreased posterior variance. It explores the theoretical conditions under which new information might fail to narrow confidence intervals.

item.title: Better Models: Worse Tools
item.description: The author discusses a regression where newer Claude models, specifically Opus 4.8 and Sonnet 5, are more prone to generating malformed tool calls compared to their predecessors. He explains that tool calling relies on text-based signals and emphasizes that despite model advancements, schema compliance for structured outputs remains a significant challenge.

item.title: Combined 1D and 2D Barcodes
item.description: The author explores the transition from traditional 1D barcodes to 2D QR codes by creating a hybrid design. By embedding a UPC within a QR code, the system allows for dual-mode scanning depending on the proximity of the reading device.

item.title: Swimming Pools, Pee, and Trying to Delete Your Data From the Internet
item.description: The article uses the analogy of urinating in a swimming pool to explain the near-impossibility of completely deleting one's personal data from the internet. It highlights how once information is shared or copied, it becomes permanently diffused across the digital ecosystem.

item.title: The Life and Times of Maxis, Part 1: SimEverything
item.description: This article explores the early history of Maxis Software and the visionary thinking of its co-founder, Will Wright. It highlights the company's unique approach to simulation games and the role of gaming enthusiasts in preserving the history of the medium.

item.title: The Fall and Rise of Screwworm
item.description: This article explores the historical impact and life cycle of the screwworm, a devastating parasite that affected livestock across North America. It details how these pests seasonally migrated from southern regions, highlighting their historical prevalence before eradication efforts.

item.title: How did we conclude that CcNamespace.dll was the ringleader of a group of DLLs that unloaded prematurely?
item.description: This post explains the investigative process used to identify CcNamespace.dll as the primary cause behind the premature unloading of a group of DLLs. It highlights the importance of analyzing contextual clues to diagnose complex system behavior issues.

item.title: Pluralistic: CARDiac, syntax coloring, view source and vibe code (03 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reflects on the educational value of the 1968 CARDiac, a papercraft computer designed to teach the fundamentals of computing. He contrasts this tactile experience with his early exposure to terminal-based programming to illustrate how physical abstraction helps bridge the gap between theory and execution.

item.title: Open Source AI Gap Map
item.description: Simon Willison highlights the launch of the Open Source AI Gap Map, a non-profit initiative indexing hundreds of AI tools, models, and datasets. The project provides its underlying data in an open GitHub repository, allowing for detailed exploration and analysis.

item.title: Quoting Josh W. Comeau
item.description: Developer course creator Josh W. Comeau reports a significant decline in sales, attributing the downturn to the rise of AI. He argues that developers are hesitant to invest in new skills due to job market uncertainty and the ability of LLMs to provide personalized tutoring.

item.title: Fable's judgement
item.description: Simon Willison shares a strategy for optimizing Claude Code by empowering the Fable model to use its own judgment for task delegation. By instructing the AI to choose lower-power models for routine coding tasks, users can improve efficiency and reduce token costs.

item.title: June 2026 newsletter
item.description: Simon Willison has released his June 2026 sponsors-only newsletter, covering topics such as recent AI model developments, export restrictions, and updates to his open-source tools. The post invites new sponsors to access the current edition and provides a link to the previous month's newsletter as a preview.

item.title: Digitale Autonomie 2.0: en nu echt
item.description: Bert Hubert reflects on his keynote speech at the Surf Privacy and Security Conference, focusing on the practical steps required for digital autonomy. He emphasizes moving beyond theoretical discussions to actionable implementation strategies for a more autonomous digital future.

item.title: Understanding is the new bottleneck
item.description: The author argues that human understanding of AI-generated code remains critical, shifting from a role of simple verification to active participation. By utilizing techniques like code explainer docs, quizzes, and micro-worlds, developers can maintain the context necessary to guide creative iteration alongside AI agents.

item.title: This Page Left Intentionally Blank
item.description: The author discusses the aesthetic and philosophical value of the 'This Page Intentionally Left Blank' project, reflecting on the concept of intentional emptiness in the age of generative AI. Inspired by historical print practices, the author creates their own blank page as a deliberate act of simplicity and quietness on the web.

item.title: Bring Back Crappy Forums
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.description: This article explores the decline of traditional web forums and reflects on why these niche, community-driven platforms often fostered deeper connections than modern social media. It examines the history of forums like Usenet and questions whether the transition to current social platforms has come at the cost of meaningful online interaction.

item.title: The case of the thread executing from an unloaded third-party DLL
item.description: This post discusses a technical debugging scenario involving a thread that continues to execute code from a DLL after it has been unloaded. It highlights a common pitfall in Windows development where memory management and thread synchronization overlap.

item.title: This blog is written in en-GB
item.description: The author defends their decision to write in en-GB, emphasizing that their blog is a personal space reflecting their cultural background. They argue that specific cultural references are intentional and reject the pressure to homogenize content for a global audience.

item.title: Pluralistic: The difference between "today's task" and "accretive work" (02 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow distinguishes between two modes of productivity: 'today's tasks' and 'accretive work.' He illustrates this using the concept of 'reverse centaurs' to explain why programmers experience AI-driven automation so differently depending on whether they control the tool or are controlled by it.

item.title: FBI Seizes NetNut Proxy Platform, Popa Botnet
item.description: The FBI, in collaboration with private industry partners, has seized domains linked to the NetNut residential proxy service. This enforcement action follows reports connecting the platform to the Popa botnet, which compromised millions of devices without user consent.

item.title: llm-coding-agent 0.1a0
item.description: Simon Willison has released an alpha version of llm-coding-agent, a new tool built upon his LLM library that functions as a coding agent. The agent was developed using iterative prompts and test-driven development, and it is now available for users to install and test via PyPI.

item.title: Using DSPy to evaluate and improve Datasette Agent's SQL system prompts
item.description: Simon Willison uses the DSPy framework to systematically evaluate and optimize the system prompts for the Datasette Agent. By running automated research tasks, the process identified specific issues with schema listing and column guessing, leading to actionable improvements for SQL query generation.

item.title: Understand to participate
item.description: This post discusses Geoffrey Litt's perspective on the necessity of maintaining a deep understanding of code when working with AI coding agents. It warns against accruing cognitive debt and emphasizes that human fluency is essential for active participation in the creative AI-assisted development process.

item.title: Text AI watermarks will always be trivial to remove
item.description: The article argues that AI-generated text watermarks are fundamentally ineffective and easy to circumvent. It suggests that technical limitations make it impossible to guarantee the permanence of these markers against determined users.

item.title: Bulkdatasets AIVD en MIVD: de schaduw geheime dienst
item.description: A new research report reveals that the Dutch intelligence agencies AIVD and MIVD handle massive bulk datasets, often containing information on millions of innocent citizens, in a careless and sometimes unlawful manner. These datasets are acquired through various sources, including foreign agencies, commercial providers, and special powers.

item.title: Summary of reading: April - June 2026
item.description: This post provides a reading digest of various books reviewed by the author between April and June 2026. The list includes a mix of historical accounts, travel memoirs, socio-political analysis, business histories, and scientific biographies.

item.title: explaining myself through stories
item.description: The author explores the limitations of language and the necessity of using narratives to express complex personal identity. By referencing literary characters, the post argues that stories provide a holistic understanding that literal descriptions or isolated facts cannot capture.

item.title: The Winning Essays for the Big Questions About AI
item.description: This article highlights the winning essays from the 'Big Questions About AI' competition. The entries cover diverse topics including strategies for pandemic prevention, the economic implications of AI automation, and potential lessons from the Hong Kong MTR business model.

item.title: The CRA is not about open source
item.description: The Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) is fundamentally a product-safety regulation for manufactured goods, rather than a piece of legislation tailored for open-source development. It treats open-source software only as a component of regulated products, failing to address the realities of open-source maintenance, registries, or community-led development.

item.title: DNA Sequence Alignment and Kings
item.description: This article explores the connection between the central Delannoy numbers and chess movements, specifically how they calculate paths for a king on a board. It further discusses the application of these mathematical concepts to DNA sequence alignment.

item.title: It rather involved being on the other side of this airtight hatchway: Changing administrative settings
item.description: This post explains the security concept of an 'airtight hatchway,' illustrating why administrative privilege boundaries are difficult to cross. It highlights that gaining elevated access from within a restricted environment is a fundamental security challenge.

item.title: 2026 mid-year link clearance
item.description: This post serves as a mid-year administrative update for The Old New Thing blog. It marks the periodic clearing of accumulated links and bookmarks, acting as a recurring housekeeping entry.

item.title: Pluralistic: Technocarcinization (01 Jul 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow uses the biological concept of 'carcinization'—where disparate species evolve into crabs—as a metaphor for the current state of the tech industry. He argues that major platforms are converging into a singular, highly controlling, and surveillance-heavy model reminiscent of Facebook, effectively losing their unique operational identities.

item.title: Quoting Anthropic
item.description: Simon Willison shares a brief update regarding Anthropic's announcement that the U.S. Department of Commerce has lifted export controls on the Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 models. Access to these generative AI services is expected to be restored shortly.

item.title: Weekly Update 510: Live From Mallorca with Scott Helme
item.description: Troy Hunt shares a retrospective on his collaboration with Scott Helme, specifically focusing on the eight-year anniversary of the 'Why no HTTPS?' project. The initiative was designed to encourage companies to adopt transport layer security by highlighting those that had not yet implemented it.

item.title: Grant Sanderson – AI and the future of math
item.description: Grant Sanderson discusses how the intersection of AI and mathematics serves as a primary frontier for the emergence of superintelligence. The conversation explores the future impact of automated reasoning on how we conduct and perceive mathematical discovery.

item.title: Data-directed programming in Haskell (SICP 2.4.3)
item.description: This post explores the concept of data-directed programming in Haskell, using complex numbers as a practical example. It demonstrates how to handle data represented in different formats, such as rectangular and polar coordinates, within a unified system.

item.title: Taking Roads and Bridges literally
item.description: The author reflects on the 'Roads and Bridges' metaphor used to describe open-source software, arguing that voluntary funding models are insufficient for critical infrastructure. By examining actual civil engineering standards, the article highlights the need for institutionalized, mandatory inspection and maintenance regimes rather than reliance on philanthropic 'Adopt-a-Highway' style contributions.

item.title: Notes from June 2026
item.description: This monthly update highlights the author's professional project launches at Ghost and creative coding work for Taper magazine. It also compiles critical perspectives on the ethical challenges of generative AI and discussions regarding open-source labor practices.

item.title: Distinguishing variables from parameters
item.description: This article explores the often confusing distinction between variables and parameters in mathematics. It clarifies that while both can change, they function differently within the scope of a function's behavior.

item.title: Silver Rectangles and the Ways of Kings
item.description: This article explores the geometric properties of silver rectangles, drawing a parallel to the well-known golden rectangle. It explains the mathematical derivation of the ratios that define these shapes, showing how their proportions remain consistent when squares are added or removed.

item.title: Derivative equals inverse
item.description: This article explores a unique mathematical problem involving a function where its derivative is equal to its inverse. It highlights that this specific differential equation cannot be solved using standard classroom techniques and requires unconventional analytical approaches.

item.title: A compatibility note on the abuse of Windows window class extra bytes
item.description: This post discusses the technical implications and compatibility issues surrounding the misuse of extra bytes in Windows window classes. It warns against hiding private data in these slots, as such practices can lead to system instability or conflicts with Windows updates.

item.title: The evolution of window and class extra bytes in Windows
item.description: This post discusses the historical development and intended usage of window and class extra bytes within the Windows operating system architecture. It highlights how naming conventions serve as a key indicator for these specific memory structures.

item.title: Book Review: Fake Creativity by Blake Loch ★★★☆☆
item.description: This blog post reviews the self-published novel 'Fake Creativity' by Blake Loch, which explores themes of paranoia and AI-driven plagiarism. The story follows an author questioning the authenticity of his own creative process as he grapples with the influence of technology.

item.title: Pluralistic: Jo Walton's "Everybody's Perfect" (30 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow reviews Jo Walton's new novel, 'Everybody's Perfect,' praising her unique ability to write profound and beautiful stories. The post highlights the author's consistent literary brilliance and situates her latest work within her broader, critically acclaimed body of writing.

item.title: The Dating App Plot Device
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: This article explores the inherent conflict in dating app business models between helping users find love versus maximizing time on the platform. The author observes that these apps commodify the search for partners by creating an illusion of perfection, ultimately resulting in a cycle of continuous monetization.

item.title: Nano Banana 2 Lite
item.description: Simon Willison shares his hands-on experience with the Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image model, Google's new cost-effective and high-speed image generator. He tests the model with a 'Where's Waldo'-style prompt and evaluates the quality and output consistency compared to previous versions.

item.title: What's new in Claude Sonnet 5
item.description: Simon Willison examines the technical updates in the new Claude Sonnet 5 model, highlighting its performance parity with Opus 4.8 and changes to API parameters. Key takeaways include the introduction of a new tokenizer that effectively increases costs by 30% and the default enabling of adaptive thinking features.

item.title: The AI Compass
item.description: The AI Compass is a political compass-style quiz that categorizes users into one of 30 archetypes based on their views on AI ethics and technology. The tool is implemented as a simple, build-free React application, reflecting the author's hands-on approach to AI.

item.title: Have your agent record video demos of its work with shot-scraper video
item.description: Simon Willison introduces the 'shot-scraper video' command, which uses Playwright to generate automated video demos of web application routines. This tool helps coding agents demonstrate their progress by executing a storyboard defined in a YAML file.

item.title: shot-scraper 1.10
item.description: The shot-scraper tool has been updated to version 1.10. The major addition is the 'video storyboard' feature, which allows users to record automated video demos of software agents in action.

item.title: HTML table extractor
item.description: Simon Willison has introduced a new browser-based tool that extracts HTML tables from pasted rich text and converts them into various formats like Markdown, CSV, and JSON. The update also adds functionality to fetch and parse tables directly from Wikipedia pages using their API.

item.title: My favorite keyboards
item.description: This article explores the author's personal preferences and reviews of various keyboard models. It details the specific features and tactile experiences that define the author's favorite typing tools.

item.title: Notes from Bryan Cantrill’s “Intelligence is not Enough”
item.description: This post reflects on Bryan Cantrill’s talk about the engineering challenges at Oxide, arguing that solving critical, unprecedented problems requires human values like resilience and teamwork rather than raw intelligence alone. It emphasizes that character and collaboration are essential for breakthroughs where traditional knowledge or synthetic intelligence fails.

item.title: Unbundling the standard library
item.description: The article explores the shifting boundary between compiler-level built-ins and standard libraries, using the Haskell GHC 10.2 update and Ruby's gemification as examples. It highlights how these shifting lines create complexities for vulnerability management and software bill of materials (SBOM) accuracy when libraries exist in both the language distribution and as standalone packages.

item.title: Who you gonna believe: Grok or the docs?
item.description: This post examines the inconsistencies between documentation and AI-generated outputs when using the calculator utility 'bc'. It highlights how large language models like Grok may hallucinate features that do not exist in standard POSIX versions of the software.

item.title: Pluralistic: Gemini is better than search because Google enshittified search (29 Jun 2026)
item.source: Pluralistic: Daily links from Cory Doctorow
item.description: Cory Doctorow critiques how Google's reliance on AI-generated search summaries undermines the open web and creator incentives. He argues that users prefer these summaries despite their inaccuracy because Google's search experience has significantly degraded.

item.title: I turned my prologue into a short video
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The author shares a new approach to book promotion by adapting their book's prologue into a short video format. This strategy addresses the difficulty of writing a full manuscript by focusing on smaller, engaging content pieces.

item.title: Count the number of Safari tabs
item.description: This post provides a quick one-line AppleScript command to count the total number of open tabs in the Safari browser. It is a brief technical tip for users who want to programmatically audit their browser tab usage.

item.title: Ornith-1.0: Self-Scaffolding LLMs for Agentic Coding
item.description: Ornith-1.0 is a new open-weights model series from DeepReinforce designed for agentic coding tasks, built upon Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5 architectures. The author highlights the model's high performance on coding benchmarks and demonstrates its practical utility through successful tool-use tasks.

item.title: Hack Your Summer
item.description: Hack Your Summer is a four-week, high-velocity sprint initiative designed to help students build real-world projects amidst a shortage of traditional internships. The program connects participants with mentors and peers to create a portfolio of public-facing work to impress future employers.

item.title: Working around dragons with the Lemote Yeeloong laptop and OpenBSD
item.description: This article explores the historical and technical aspects of the Lemote Yeeloong laptop, which features a MIPS-based 'Godson' processor. The author examines the challenges of running OpenBSD on this niche hardware and discusses the linguistic and cultural origins of the processor's naming.

item.title: Brace expansion tree
item.description: This post analyzes a complex bash command that utilizes brace expansion to generate thirty distinct English words. It breaks down the syntax of the one-liner to demonstrate how nested shell expansions function.

item.title: Examining circuit boards from the Space Shuttle's I/O Processor
item.description: This article examines the hardware architecture of the Space Shuttle's I/O Processor, detailing its role in managing communication between the CPU and vehicle sensors. The author explains the function of specific circuit boards, known as 'pages,' and describes how the processor utilized early multi-threading and physical microcode fuses.

item.title: Book Review: The Hotel Avocado by Bob Mortimer ★★☆☆☆
item.description: Terence Eden shares his disappointment with Bob Mortimer's 'The Hotel Avocado,' finding the sequel significantly inferior to the original. He notes that the charm of the first book has devolved into clichéd storytelling and excessive violence.

item.title: Review: Gamrombo PS5 controller - including Linux set up ★★★★☆
item.description: This review evaluates a budget-friendly third-party Gamrombo PS5 controller, highlighting its cost-effectiveness and unique lighting features. It also provides practical guidance on configuring the device for use on Linux systems.

item.title: Arp 38: not that peculiar
item.description: This post provides an astronomical observation and imaging report of the spiral galaxy Arp 38. The author analyzes the visual structure of the galaxy, noting the absence of a companion as originally described by Arp, and details the specific equipment and processing workflow used to capture the image.

item.title: The Laziest Generation
item.source: Software and Tech stories from an Insider - iDiallo.com
item.description: The article uses a satirical tone to critique the common generational trope that blames modern housing unaffordability on 'reckless' spending habits like avocado toast. It highlights the stark reality of skyrocketing real estate prices compared to previous decades, demonstrating that the barrier to homeownership has fundamentally changed.
